item.title: 404 and robots
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
404 and robots.txt

404.html

The 404.html template fills the content block of the base template with the 404.html partial. The content is provided by the 404-content.html partial and contains:

  • the translated “page not found” heading and back link
  • optionally an error image, if the site parameter errorimg is set — the image source is the site parameter logo

Site parameters

Parameter Type Default Purpose
errorimg bool false Show the error image
logo string — Image URL used for the error image

robots.txt

The robots.txt template is enabled with enableRobotsTXT = true in the site configuration. It renders:

item.title: ActivityPub actor
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
ActivityPub actor

The activity-pub-actor output format renders an ActivityStreams Person object (actor.json) describing the site owner for static ActivityPub discovery.

Reference implementation: christianmahnke/layouts/_default/single.activity-pub-actor.json. The theme ships no ActivityPub templates — copy or adapt that template if the format is needed.

Output

{
  "@context": "https://www.w3.org/ns/activitystreams",
  "type": "Person",
  "url": "https://example.org/",
  "discoverable": true,
  "name": "Example site"
}

Depending on the [params.activitypub] configuration, id/preferredUsername, outbox, icon, image and an attachment list of PropertyValue link entries are added.

Site parameters

Parameter Type Default Purpose
params.activitypub.author string — Username used for id (<baseURL>@<author>) and preferredUsername
params.activitypub.outbox string — Outbox filename appended to the base URL, e.g. outbox.json
params.activitypub.icon string — Asset path resolved with resources.Get for the icon image
params.activitypub.image string — Asset path resolved with resources.Get for the image
params.activitypub.links map — Name to HTML link mapping rendered as attachment
params.Description string — Rendered as summary if set

Enabling

[mediaTypes]
  [mediaTypes."application/activity+json"]
    suffixes = ["json"]

[outputFormats]
  [outputFormats.activity-pub-actor]
    mediaType = "application/activity+json"
    isPlainText = true
    isHTML = false
    baseName = "actor"
    notAlternative = true

[params.activitypub]
  author = "example"
  icon = "images/logo.png"
  image = "images/background.jpg"
  outbox = "outbox.json"

Enable it per page via outputs, the generated file is available as /page/actor.json.

item.title: ActivityPub outbox
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
ActivityPub outbox

The activity-pub-outbox output format renders an ActivityStreams OrderedCollection (outbox.json) listing recent posts as Create/Note objects.

Reference implementation: christianmahnke/layouts/_default/home.activity-pub-outbox.json. The theme ships no ActivityPub templates — copy or adapt that template if the format is needed.

Output

{
  "@context": "https://www.w3.org/ns/activitystreams",
  "type": "OrderedCollection",
  "totalItems": 2,
  "orderedItems": [
    {
      "type": "Create",
      "actor": "https://example.org@example",
      "object": {
        "type": "Note",
        "content": "<a href=\"https://example.org/post/my-page/\">My page</a>",
        "to": "https://www.w3.org/ns/activitystreams#Public",
        "published": "2024-04-15T13:58:44+02:00"
      }
    }
  ]
}

Pages come from section post and exclude pages with displayinlist: false. The actor/attributedTo fields are only rendered if [params.activitypub] author is set.

item.title: Base template
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
Base template

The base template _default/baseof.html defines the common page skeleton: <head> (via the html/head/meta.html, links.html, style.html and script.html partials), the site header with top navigation, the <main> element and the footer.

Blocks

Custom templates override the following blocks:

Block Purpose
title <title> content, defaults to the page title (plus the slogan on the home page) — the html/head/title.html partial renders it
body Attributes and content at the start of <body>
main Content before the content block inside <main>
content The actual page content

item.title: BibTeX
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
BibTeX

The bibtex output format renders a per-page BibTeX citation file (citation.bib).

Reference implementation: christianmahnke/layouts/_default/single.bib. The theme ships no bibtex page template — copy or adapt that template if the format is needed.

Output

citation.bib contains a single entry, e.g.:

@article{my-key,
  author = {Christian Mahnke},
  title = {My title},
  url = {https://example.org/post/my-page/},
  year = {2024},
}

If the page has no cite: true front matter, the file only contains:

% Error: BibTex export not enabled: Cannot generate BibTeX entry.

Front matter parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Purpose
cite bool yes — Set to true to enable the export, otherwise only the error comment is rendered
bibtex_key string yes — Citation key after @<type>{
authors list of maps no site author.name Maps with first and last, joined with and
doi string no — Rendered as doi = {…}
note string no — Rendered as note = {…}
description string no — Rendered as abstract = {…}
keywords string list no — Rendered as keywords = {…} (space separated)

The entry type comes from the site parameter citation.type and defaults to article. url is the permalink of the page’s html output, year and month come from the page date.

item.title: Data lists
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
Data list templates

The theme generates several JSON files used for client side search, tag relations and Wikidata integration. All of them filter out pages with displayinlist: false and — where noted — metaPage: true.

post-list.json

An index of all pages of the current language, used by client side search. Each entry contains:

Field Source
url HTML output permalink
title Page title
section Paths of all ancestor sections
path Page path
lang Language code
summary Page summary
tags Page tags, if set
date Page date, if set
outputs All output formats of the page with name and url

Pages with metaPage: true are excluded.

item.title: GeoJSON
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
GeoJSON

Template: _default/section.geojson, output format geojson. It renders a section as a GeoJSON FeatureCollection — one feature per page in the section that provides GeoJSON data.

Usage

The template collects all pages of the current section with a geojson front matter parameter and renders them via the geojson/featureCollection.geojson partial, which uses the geojson/feature.geojson and geojson/popupContent.html partials per page.

A page needs at least a marker definition, e.g.:

---
title: A place
geojson:
  coordinates: [10.0, 53.55]
---

The rendered popup content is the page content, an HTML preview can be generated separately (geojson/popupContent-preview.html).

item.title: IIIF templates
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
IIIF templates

The IIIF related output formats generate IIIF Presentation API resources. All details about configuration and front matter are documented in the IIIF section, this page lists the templates involved.

Template Output format Purpose
_default/home.iiif-collection.json iiif-collection Collection of all manifests, merging pages of all languages
_default/term.iiif-collection.json iiif-collection Collection for a term or section page
_default/single.iiif-manifest.json iiif-manifest Manifest for a single page
_default/section.iiif-manifest.json iiif-manifest Manifest for a section page

All of them delegate to the iiif/3/ partials (and iiif/4/ for the Presentation API 4 draft). Pages with displayinlist: false are excluded from collections.

item.title: Linkset
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
Linkset

The linkset output format advertises a W3C linkset (application/linkset+json) for a page. The theme only registers the format and advertises it in the document head — the content is entirely site specific and rendered by a site-provided template.

Output format definition

From the theme’s hugo.toml (merged into every site using the theme):

[mediaTypes."application/linkset+json"]
  suffixes = ["json"]

[outputFormats]
  [outputFormats.linkset]
    mediaType = "application/linkset+json"
    baseName = "linkset"
    isPlainText = true
    isHTML = false
    rel = "linkset"

The rel = "linkset" value is what makes the document head emit <link rel="linkset"> instead of the default rel="alternate". The output file is linkset.json next to the page.

item.title: LLMS
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
LLMS

The llms output format (llms.json, text/plain) is a placeholder defined in the reference configuration. Neither the theme nor the reference site ships a page template for it — do not confuse it with the llms.txt crawler hint described below.

Output format definition

From christianmahnke/config.toml:

[outputFormats]
  [outputFormats.llms]
    mediaType = "text/plain"
    baseName = "llms"
    isPlainText = true
    notAlternative = true

There is no single.llms.*, list.llms.* or similar template in layouts/. Enabling the format without providing such a template renders nothing useful; add a custom template first if the file is needed.

item.title: Metadata formats
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
Metadata output formats

The theme can generate machine readable metadata descriptions of a site or page: schema.org JSON-LD, CodeMeta for software and Linked Art for cultural heritage objects.

schemaorg

Template: _default/schema-org.json, typically applied to the home page or a section. It renders a WebSite with a Blog (hasPart) containing all BlogPosting entries of the section’s pages.

Parameters

Parameter Type Default Purpose
section string post Section the blog posts are taken from
type string Blog @type of the blog node

The author information comes from the author/authors front matter or site parameters, additional about entities are collected from the page metadata partials (metadata/schema.org/).

item.title: PDF article
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
PDF article

The pdf-article output format renders a per-page printable article variant (article.html) used as input for PDF generation.

Reference implementation: christianmahnke/layouts/_default/single.pdf-article.html with christianmahnke/layouts/_default/baseof.pdf-article.html. The theme ships no pdf-article page template — only the shared baseof.print.html base variant and the print/ partials and shortcodes — copy or adapt those templates if the format is needed.

Behavior

  • single.pdf-article.html fills the title and content blocks with the page header and the article/page.html partial.
  • baseof.pdf-article.html is a standalone skeleton: it sets author, subject and date meta tags, compiles scss/article-pdf.scss to css/article.css and loads js/print.js. Asset URLs honor the site parameter print.relative.
  • Shortcodes can provide *.pdf-article.html overrides (e.g. figure.pdf-article.html, footnote.pdf-article.html, gallery.pdf-article.html), the reference site uses them to produce PDF friendly markup.

The print output format is intentionally not documented here.

item.title: QR codes
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
QR code templates

The qrcode output format generates a small JSON file per page describing the data to encode as a QR code — the actual image generation happens client side. Templates: _default/single.qrcode.json (pages) and _default/section.qrcode.json (sections).

Output

{
  "url": "https://example.org/page/",
  "color": "#000000",
  "icon": "…",
  "iconColor": "…"
}
  • url is the permalink of the page’s HTML output. If the page defines aliases, url becomes an array containing the permalink plus all alias URLs
  • the remaining fields are optional and only rendered if the corresponding front matter parameters are set

Front matter parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Purpose
aliases string list no — Additional URLs to encode
qr-color string no — QR code color
qr-icon string no — Icon (image) overlaid on the code
qr-icon-color string no — Color of the overlaid icon

Enabling

The output format is defined in the site configuration (see the example site):

item.title: Redirects
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
Redirect template

Template: redirect/single.html. Renders a page as an immediate client side redirect using a <meta http-equiv="refresh"> tag and a canonical link, following Dan North’s approach to Hugo redirects.

The page is marked with <meta name="robots" content="noindex"> so search engines ignore it.

Front matter parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Purpose
target string yes — URL to redirect to

Usage

---
title: Old page
target: https://example.org/new-page/
---

item.title: Search page
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
Search

The search.html template renders the search page: a text input, a filter container and a result container. All actual searching happens client side with Pagefind — the index is built after Hugo runs (see pagefind-index.yaml in the theme root).

Usage

Create a page using the template via its layout front matter:

---
title: Search
layout: search
---

The page also needs the search script, either via its front matter (as the example page does) or imported by the site’s own main.ts:

item.title: Single and list templates
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
Single and list templates

_default/single.html

Renders regular pages. It only fills the title and content blocks of the base template and delegates the actual markup to the page.html partial, which renders:

  • the page title as h1.post-title
  • the page content, wrapped in a div.post with the type front matter parameter as additional CSS class
  • date and tags footer — unless the page has metaPage: true

_default/list.html

Renders section, taxonomy and term pages, as well as the home page. It delegates to the list.html partial, which:
